effect: A slow source does not prevent a useful frozen forecast publication through existing readers.
required: Snapshots never share mutable acquisition objects.
Publication callbacks are serialized and bounded to one attempt per minute; zero-model projections do not consume the publication interval.
Every previously requested station, date and provider remains acquired.
The final projection preserves original source/model values apart from added acquisition metadata.
Partial and full completeness are explicit, independent of universe completeness.
Pending forecasts, rule changes, fresh quote receipts, scoring and trade admission use the existing path.
Native receiving must show a useful latest publication while acquisition is still active.
Partial venue publications use a distinct during-acquisition-v1 stage; completed-cycle admission cannot be borrowed, and original completed-cycle admission remains available.
A partial snapshot with zero models at publication time leaves the previous latest publication intact.
Station-state JSON retains every field and row while eliminating file-sized read/write strings.

amendments.reason: Native receiving demonstrated that incremental publication still awaited whole scientific updates and venue requests.
required: Partial source laws publish without science fitting, old-outcome venue requests, quote refresh, experiments, books or allocation offers.
Existing venue participation consumers capture fresh market metadata, prices, fees and books independently.
Direct source laws and late-listing projections use their own source-projection-v1 prospective calibration cohort.
Partial source laws create immutable evidence and prospective venue grading records.
Complete acquisition retains all providers, stations and original scientific refinement and model values.
Native receiving shows a useful real-root publication while providers remain unfinished and the worker is alive.
